feedback: Written before this candidate has raced. Iteration 5 (mass 0.5 kg) is the best design: oval finish 95%, oval steering_oscillation 0.23, s-bend progress 0.72, and s-bend max_error still at the 0.06 m limit (0.063). Iteration 4 showed that the wheel_radius change lifted the oval finish rate from 65% to 80%, and iteration 5 showed that cutting mass from 0.6 to 0.5 kg lifted it again to 95%, so yaw inertia and speed were limiting the oval. Slalom is the weak point: line_loss_events rose to 1.85 in iteration 5 and 2.0 in iteration 4, while slalom progress stayed at about 0.14. Iteration 1 showed that widening the spread alone did not reduce line losses, and iteration 3 showed that seven sensors at y=0.08 m raised oscillation and lowered the oval finish rate, so the sensor fix needs to be a coverage change at the current forward offset. I kept the controller unchanged from iteration 5 so the mass change is isolated. Depending on the next race: if s-bend max_error falls below 0.06 m with steering_oscillation at or under 0.3, the inertia limit was real and the next lever is wheel_track 0.09 m for more turn authority. If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.85, the sensor coverage on alternating bends is the bottleneck, so widen the outer sensors to about ±0.045 m with the same 16 mm footprint, which keeps tape visible to about 0.0655 m offset. If steering_oscillation rises sharply while max_error does not move, the controller gain is the bottleneck, and the Integrator will retune kd and kp rather than the geometry.
requested_changes: If s-bend max_error stays at about 0.06 m while slalom line_loss_events fall below 1.0, try wheel_track 0.09 m (from 0.10 m) for more turn authority. Iteration 5 showed mass reduction helped the s-bend, and the remaining limit looks like turn rate.

If slalom line_loss_events stay near 1.85 with max_error near 0.065 m, widen the outer sensors to x = ±0.045 m, keeping the five-sensor layout, y = 0.07 m and the 16 mm footprint. Iterations 1 and 4 show that the current ±0.036 m span leaves the outer sensors blind at about 0.0565 m offset, and ±0.045 m keeps tape visible to about 0.0655 m.

Do not move sensors forward beyond y = 0.07 m again. Iteration 3 (seven sensors at y=0.08 m) raised oval steering_oscillation from about 0.28 to 0.36 and cut the oval finish rate to 35%, so extra look-ahead has not paid off.
